project: Wuxia Life P90 Medical Late-Life Design-First
description: Design-first contract stage for medical_sage_healer late-life phase — define 6 late-life branches (2 variants × 3 choices), contract, and validation shape before implementation, preserving tavern-born medical healer flavor. Assess GO/NO-GO for late-life implementation.

userStories.title: Audit medical late-life prerequisites
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want a prerequisite audit for the medical late-life stage so P90 starts from the real gating surfaces and not from assumptions.
acceptanceCriteria: Summarize existing medical route flags, markers, events, and expressions (bridge + entry + on-ramp + pressure + payoff)
Document state differences across 6 payoff choices (stats + flags + identity)
Identify what exists before late-life vs what can be reused
Compare with renown late-life to identify medical-unique opportunities and constraints
Save docs/test-reports/p90-medical-late-life-prerequisite-audit.md
Do not change runtime behavior in this story
userStories.notes: Starts from 5-stage foundation (P83-P89). 6 payoff branches = more complex than renown's 3. Must identify medical-unique flavor vs renown late-life.

userStories.title: Lock P90 scope contract
userStories.description: As a planner, I want a scope contract so P90 stays design-first and does not slip into partial implementation.
acceptanceCriteria: Limit P90 to prerequisite audit, scope contract, branch design, late-life contract, validation shape, and closure only
Define allowed layers: documentation, contract, targeted proof planning
List forbidden expansions: runtime wiring, new framework, bulk content wave, endgame design, second route, plague/pure expansion
Define 6 branches as upper bound; allow reduction if narrative value is insufficient
Save docs/test-reports/p90-medical-late-life-scope-contract.md
userStories.notes: Critical guardrail against scope creep. 6 branches is ambitious — must be honest about which ones add real value.

userStories.title: Design six late-life branches (per payoff choice)
userStories.description: As a designer, I want six distinct late-life branches (one per payoff choice) so medical late-life leverages the 2-variant × 3-choice structure for meaningful differentiation.
acceptanceCriteria: Design Compassionate A (holder / 油尽灯枯) late-life branch: core narrative + trigger + player experience
Design Compassionate B (let_go / 释然通透) late-life branch: core narrative + trigger + player experience
Design Compassionate C (legacy / 仁心传承) late-life branch: core narrative + trigger + player experience
Design Pragmatic A (holder / 声名赫赫) late-life branch: core narrative + trigger + player experience
Design Pragmatic B (breaker / 快意江湖) late-life branch: core narrative + trigger + player experience
Design Pragmatic C (master / 人情练达) late-life branch: core narrative + trigger + player experience
Six branches have meaningfully different identities (not reskinned)
Two variants have genuinely different late-life directions (not mirrored)
Each branch has tavern-born medical healer flavor adaptation
Decide: single event with 6 branches vs multi-event (recommend single auto event for boundedness)
Clearly differentiated from renown late-life (healer identity vs jianghu renown identity)
Save design document
userStories.notes: Core creative work. 6 branches = 2× renown's complexity. Must ensure compassionate vs pragmatic variants feel fundamentally different, not just labeled differently.

userStories.title: Define medical late-life contract
userStories.description: As a designer, I want an explicit late-life contract so P91 knows exactly what flags, gates, events, and player-facing meanings must be closed.
acceptanceCriteria: Define late-life checkpoint, required flags, and corresponding gate acceptance
Define late-life event structure (choice or auto; recommend auto with 6 branches)
Define stat changes, identity markers, and expression differences per branch
Define at least 3 late-life-specific player-facing signals (cost label, current goal, late-life identity, etc.)
Clarify difference between late-life vs payoff and vs generic endgame
Preserve tavern-born medical healer flavor throughout
Reserve flag interfaces for subsequent endgame / final legacy stages
Save contract to docs/PRD/p90-medical-late-life-contract.md
userStories.notes: Handoff artifact for P91 implementation. Must be unambiguous enough that P91 needs zero direction decisions.

userStories.title: Define P91 validation shape
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want the P91 validation shape fixed in advance so playable late-life work is judged against explicit expectations.
acceptanceCriteria: Define which chain nodes targeted proof must show (payoff → late-life → expression changes)
Each of 6 branches must have core node verification
Define which assertions regression tests must cover at minimum
Define what evidence counts as late-life closed
No full lifetime exhaust required
Define regression boundaries for P83/P84/P85/P87/P89 existing evidence
Compare with renown late-life (P79) test coverage to ensure medical 6-branch validation depth is sufficient
userStories.notes: Sets the bar for P91. 6 branches means more test surface than renown — must ensure coverage depth matches complexity.

userStories.title: Produce P90 closure report
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want a closure report that locks the medical late-life design-first contract and hands off to P91.
acceptanceCriteria: Save docs/test-reports/p90-medical-late-life-closure-report.md
Summarize prerequisite audit, scope contract, late-life branch design, late-life contract, validation shape
Clarify boundary with P91
List remaining deferred larger medical-expansion items
State GO / NO-GO for late-life implementation stage (with rationale either way)
If NO-GO, clearly state stopping point and why
14 closure criteria (following P88→P89 validation shape pattern)
userStories.notes: Final output. Must include explicit GO/NO-GO recommendation with clear criteria.
